data.content_ref: inline:The target's evidentiary test for independence is unsound. It claims truly independent failures 'will follow a Poisson distribution over time and space,' but this is only valid under a homogeneous Poisson process — a special case requiring constant failure rates and no seasonal/diurnal load variation. Real small, independently operated services have failure rates that vary with traffic patterns, deployment schedules, and operator business hours, so non-Poisson behavior does not evidence a shared cause. The target thus misclassifies routine non-stationary but genuinely independent failures as correlated, undermining its central distinction. Moreover, its own counterconditions concede this weakness: a slow-burn shared-cause degradation (the listed countercondition) can also manifest as temporally staggered, apparently uncorrelated failures, so the target lacks any positive evidence that survives its own listed defeaters.
